title: Elderflower Cordial
subtitle: The classic British summer cordial, fragrant, floral, and very versatile
excerpt: Elderflower cordial is made by steeping freshly picked elderflower heads in a hot sugar syrup for 24 hours. Dilute 1:10 with cold water or sparkling water. Makes about 2 litres.
sourceNotes: Classic British forager's cordial. Pam Corbin, Preserves. The window for elderflowers is narrow, early June to early July depending on the year. Flowers must be used within 24 hours of picking.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in ice cube trays or small containers for up to 12 months.

content.text: Elderflower cordial is one of the strongest arguments for seasonal foraging,  the flavour of good elderflower cordial made from freshly picked heads is completely different from any commercial version. The flowers steep for 24 hours in hot sugar syrup, which extracts the fragrance without bitterness. Makes about 2 litres.

Pick elderflowers from trees away from roadsides and agricultural spray zones. Use flowers that are fully open and smell strongly of flowers,  not ones that smell slightly like cat urine (a sign of over-ripeness). Use within 24 hours of picking.

items.prepNote: freshly picked, stems trimmed to 2 cm
zest pared in strips; juice reserved
extends shelf life; available from home-brew shops

content.text: Bring the water and sugar to a simmer in the pan, stirring until the sugar dissolves completely. Remove from the heat.
Add the elderflower heads, lemon zest strips, lemon juice, and citric acid if using to the hot syrup. Stir, cover, and leave to steep at room temperature for 24 hours.
Strain through a fine sieve lined with muslin into a large jug, pressing firmly on the flowers to extract all the liquid. Pour into sterilised bottles and seal. Refrigerate once opened.

items.symptom: Cordial ferments and becomes fizzy in the bottle
items.cause: Yeast from the flowers is actively fermenting the sugar. More common without citric acid.
items.fix: Use citric acid to help preserve. Store in the fridge rather than at room temperature. Cordial without citric acid keeps only 2 weeks in the fridge.

items.cause: Over-ripe flowers used, or steeped for too long.
items.fix: Pick flowers that smell strongly floral. Don't steep for more than 24 hours, longer extraction increases bitterness.

items.cause: Flowers were past their best or picked too early.
items.fix: Use flowers at peak, fully open, fragrant, and in the first week of their season. Closed buds have much less flavour.
Line the sieve with a double layer of muslin. A slight haze is not a problem, it's aesthetic only.

content.text: With citric acid: keeps 3 to 4 weeks in the fridge. Without: 1 to 2 weeks in the fridge. Freeze in small portions for up to 12 months.
